thread.title: Trade war’s ‘nuclear option’ could be bad for Apple, Amazon: strategist - MarketWatch

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Trade war’s ‘nuclear option’ could be bad for Apple, Amazon: strategist - MarketWatch
text:
Stock market bulls have met trade-war headlines largely head on this year—pausing at times to snort and paw the ground before charging right through.
But as investors weigh up the White House’s latest battle with China on trade, some are warning that this time, things could be different. Among them is our call of the day from Michael O’Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading, who warns of dire consequences if China takes the “nuclear option” of restricting sales of materials, equipment and other key parts of U.S. manufacturers’ supply chain.
“The disruption it would cause for the global economy and financial markets would be astounding. It would shift from a trade war to economic warfare by means of a scorched earth approach,” O’Rourke told clients in a note.
Apple AAPL, +0.67% would be one of the big losers under those circumstances, he said.
Opinion: Apple Watch is safe, but China tariffs could still hit other consumer tech products
“The number one product the U.S. imports from China is cellphones, a large portion of which are iPhones. Once the tariffs start effecting the prices of Apple’s products and Main Street America, as well as corporate profits, the effects of the tariffs will feel much more tangible,” says O’Rourke.
See Also This Bicyclist Just Pedaled 184 MPH. Really. × Apple’s stock initially rallied Monday, spurred by news the iWatch and wireless earbuds were excluded from U.S. tariffs on $200 billion in Chinese goods. But the shares turned down once fears about China’s retaliation took over and Apple ended the session down 2.7%.
Read: Latest U.S. tariffs won’t affect Apple, but China’s retaliation might
Lots of retailers, such as Amazon AMZN, +1.70% and Walmart WMT, +0.64% also have goods that will be in the tariff firing line, he said.
As for those who argue that China would be crazy to go “nuclear” and blow up its relationships with U.S. companies, O’Rourke says the country can simply argue that “it didn’t start this war.”

The market The S&P SPX, +0.71% , Dow DJIA, +0.86% and Nasdaq COMP, +0.99% COMP, +0.99% are all modestly higher.
Gold GCU8, -0.18% and crude US:CLU8 are softer, while the dollar DXY, +0.14% is holding steady.
Europe SXXP, +0.11% is mostly firmer and Asia stocks had an upbeat day with the Shanghai Composite SHCOMP, +1.82% rebounding from a nearly four-year low.

The buzz China responded, sort of, to the $200 billion in tariffs on its imports announced late Monday by the Trump administration . The Commerce Ministry said on its website that it “has no choice but to undertake synchronous retaliation.” Meanwhile, Alibaba’s BABA, -1.76% chairman Jack Ma warned that the spat between the two countries could last two decades .

Cannibas cultivator Tilray TLRY, +26.42% has won approval from the DEA to import a pot product from Canada to test how effective it is in treating a neurological disorder that affects millions of Americans.
Alphabet’s Google GOOGL, +1.11% is teaming up with a big auto alliance to provide infotainment systems for their cars and Amazon AMZN, +1.70% reportedly plans to launch an Alexa-powered microwave and other gadgets.
“Black Mirror” and other hits brought home the Emmys on Monday night for Netflix NFLX, +3.51% which tied with AT&T’s T, +0.65% HBO for most nominations this year. Amazon AMZN, +1.70% also didn’t come out too shabby with wins for “The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel.”
